content:
mike: Quick heads-up — our sampleapp rerank flow is returning scrambled ranks after a retry burst from the Node SDK. Repro is pretty consistent when batching size >= 8 and one of the downstream requests times out.

mike: Minimal repro (Node):
```js
// batchHelper.js (client v0.9.2)
const ids = docs.map((d, i) => `doc-${i}`);
const payload = { vectors: docs.map(d => padVec(d.vec, 1536)), ids };
await client.rerank.batch({ model: 'open-sim-rerank', body: payload });
```

mike: Observed behavior: when a retry happens the API returns items with correct scores but the response array order doesn't match the original ids array. The client then maps scores back by index and messes up the top-k.

sasha: :eyes: can you paste the raw request/response pairing (headers + server logs)?

mike: Yea — server log snippet: 
```
[2026-02-10T15:22:01Z] incoming batch id=batch-7 size=10 client=mike-node-0.9.2
[2026-02-10T15:22:01Z] dispatch shard=rerank-3 seq=42
[2026-02-10T15:22:02Z] timeout waiting for model response seq=42
[2026-02-10T15:22:02Z] fallback: retrying to shard rerank-2 seq=42 retry=1
[2026-02-10T15:22:03Z] response sent seq=42 idempotency=none order_preserve=false
```

mike: Response body (trimmed):
```
{ scores: [0.98,0.65,0.63, ...], ids: ["doc-3","doc-0","doc-7", ...] }
```

mike: So the server is returning ids but the SDK assumes stable index mapping and reconstructs by index. The Node batching helper currently loses the explicit ids -> score mapping on retry.

olga: Huh — two bugs colliding: (1) Node SDK retry path drops idempotency header so server treats it like a fresh request and reorders during internal shard fallback; (2) batch helper normalizer expects position-stable responses instead of matching by returned id.

olga: Quick fix: always attach `x-idempotency-key` per batch and, on response, match scores by `ids` field (fall back to index only if ids missing). I'll sketch a tiny PR for the helper.

jordan: Also saw a variant where padVec returned `null` entries when a doc vec was shorter — server then coerced null->0 and that shifted lengths, leading to the "vectors must be length 1536" errors for some shards.

mike: Yup I hit that too. Repro: one doc with missing embedding => padVec produced `[1.2, null, 0, ...]` => server coerced and later quantization kernel exploded on a retry path.

sasha: We should add pre-send validation in the helper: assert all numbers, length exactly model_dim, no NaN/null, and a debug flag to dump offending doc ids. Tiny middleware.

devex-bot: Reminder: 1) open a bug (DX-?) for SDK retry idempotency; 2) add unit tests for batch order-by-id path; 3) schedule small perf test so we don't regress stream behavior.

mike: I'll open the bug and initial PR. PR will: attach idempotency header, change response mapping to id->score, add validation error with helpful message like "vector #{id} length=1528 expected=1536 — padVec returned malformed vector".

olga: Thanks. One UX note — sampleapp's quickstart template silently swallows idempotency header to keep examples short. We should add a tiny comment so users hitting retries in prod don't get burned.

jordan: I'm going to add a failing test in rust-sdk and python-sdk parity suite: create a retry stub that returns reordered ids on second call. Both SDKs should map by returned ids, not by index.

sasha: Can we add a lightweight lint step in the sampleapp CI that runs a 100-req burst through rerank to catch this class of ordering issues? Cheap and catches shard fallback ordering.

mike: Good call. I'll add a github action that runs locally against the dockerized localstack of the inference runtime.

olga: For short-term hotfix, set Node SDK default retry to 1 and linear backoff to 200ms -> 400ms and document idempotency header requirement. Longer-term: make retry idempotent by default for batch endpoints.

mike: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/1423 — placeholder, not final. Assigning to @olga for review.

olga: Reviewing tomorrow AM. Thanks for the detailed repro — saved a customer call. :thumbsup:
